identification.summary: The name Daffodil Gust, and any Microsoft mapping of it to Stealth Falcon, FruityArmor or Project Raven, could not be confirmed in search; the entries below describe the publicly reported Stealth Falcon/FruityArmor activity. Citizen Lab reported on a spyware campaign it named Stealth Falcon against Emirati journalists and dissidents, dated 2016-05-29, with activity dating from 2012 [S2]. Kaspersky tracked a Windows zero-day (CVE-2016-3393) used by an actor it called FruityArmor, patched in October 2016 [S3]. Check Point Research attributed a 2025 WebDAV zero-day campaign (CVE-2025-33053) to Stealth Falcon, also tracked as FruityArmor [S6].
identification.firstObserved: 2012 (earliest activity in Citizen Lab's Stealth Falcon reporting) [S2]
identification.notes: The vendor reports cited here use Stealth Falcon and FruityArmor; whether those clusters are identical to Daffodil Gust is not shown in the sources reviewed [S3][S6]. Amnesty's Claudio Guarnieri is reported to have concluded Stealth Falcon and Project Raven are the same group, as relayed by secondary coverage [S8]. Project Raven (Reuters reporting) describes an operation staffed by former US intelligence personnel [S4]; treat the Raven link as a reported overlap, not a vendor-confirmed merge.

attribution.sponsor: Possibly the United Arab Emirates (circumstantial, per Citizen Lab; Reuters reporting on Project Raven) [S2][S4]
attribution.confidence: Citizen Lab did not name the UAE as the perpetrator and described the link as circumstantial [S2]. Reuters reported (January 2019) that Project Raven worked for UAE intelligence services via the contractor DarkMatter, which DarkMatter was reported to deny [S4]. No government attribution was found in the sources reviewed.
attribution.basis: Citizen Lab's 2016 finding of targeting of Emirati dissidents and journalists, with circumstantial links to the UAE government [S2]; Reuters reporting on Project Raven and reported overlap with Stealth Falcon targeting/infrastructure via secondary sources [S4][S8]; Check Point attribution of the 2025 campaign to Stealth Falcon (secondary summaries cite TTP, infrastructure and code overlaps) [S6]. Note: the 2021 US DOJ resolution concerned three former US personnel working for a UAE company and did not itself name Stealth Falcon in the coverage seen [S5].

objectives: Espionage: Citizen Lab documented surveillance of Emirati journalists, activists and dissidents [S2]; Check Point reports government and defense targeting in the Middle East and Africa in the 2025 campaign [S6]. Reuters reported targets of Project Raven included Qatar's emir, a senior Turkish official and a Yemeni human-rights activist [S4].

targeting.notes: 2016: Citizen Lab's work, mainly Emirati dissidents and journalists [S2]. 2016 FruityArmor victims reported in Thailand, Iran, Algeria, Yemen, Saudi Arabia and Sweden [S3]. 2019 ESET: few observed attacks in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Thailand and one at a Middle Eastern diplomatic mission in the Netherlands [S7]. 2025: government and defense targets in Turkey, Qatar, Egypt and Yemen [S6].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with fake personas, malicious URL shorteners and booby-trapped documents (2016) [S2]. Use of zero-days: a Windows font/privilege-escalation exploit CVE-2016-3393 following browser exploitation, with a PowerShell- and WMI-based platform [S3]; CVE-2025-33053, a WebDAV working-directory remote code execution flaw triggered via a crafted shortcut/.url file pulling malware from an attacker-run WebDAV server, patched 2025-06-10 [S6]. Custom malware: Win32/StealthFalcon backdoor (ESET, 2019) that abuses Windows BITS for C2 [S7]; Horus Agent, a custom implant built on the open-source Mythic framework (2025, per secondary summaries of Check Point) [S6]. Project Raven reportedly used the Karma iPhone exploit tool [S4].

campaigns.name: Stealth Falcon spyware against Emirati dissidents
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab (2016-05-29) described a campaign since 2012 using fake-persona phishing and malicious documents; a UK-based journalist, Rori Donaghy, received a spyware email in November 2015 [S2].

campaigns.name: FruityArmor zero-day CVE-2016-3393
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky reported a Windows privilege-escalation exploit hidden in a TTF font, used after browser exploitation, patched as MS16-120 [S3].

campaigns.name: Reuters Project Raven reporting
campaigns.summary: Reuters reported an Abu Dhabi unit of Emirati officials and former US intelligence operatives using the Karma tool against iPhones, paid via DarkMatter [S4].

campaigns.name: ESET Win32/StealthFalcon backdoor
campaigns.summary: ESET described a backdoor attributed to the group using BITS, apparently created in 2015, with a few targets in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Thailand and the Netherlands [S7].

campaigns.name: US DOJ resolution with three former US personnel
campaigns.summary: Three former US intelligence/military personnel entered deferred prosecution agreements over zero-click hacking services for a UAE company, with a reported USD 1.68 million payment [S5].

campaigns.name: CVE-2025-33053 WebDAV zero-day campaign
campaigns.summary: Check Point Research reported Stealth Falcon exploiting CVE-2025-33053 to deliver the Horus Agent against targets in Turkey, Qatar, Egypt and Yemen; Microsoft patched on 2025-06-10. The March 2025 start date is from a secondary summary [S6].

diamond.adversary: Actor reported as Stealth Falcon/FruityArmor, with circumstantial UAE links; possibly overlapping with a contractor-supported unit reported as Project Raven [S2][S4].
diamond.capability: Zero-days, custom backdoors and implants, phishing, reported iPhone exploitation tooling [S3][S4][S6][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Attacker-controlled WebDAV servers (2025) [S6]; malicious URL shorteners and fake-persona accounts (2016) [S2]; BITS-based C2 channel (2019) [S7]. Specific domains/IPs not captured.
diamond.victim: Emirati and regional dissidents, journalists, diplomats, government and defense entities [S2][S6][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Surveillance of domestic critics and regional rivals aligned with UAE state interests, as reported [S2][S4].
diamond.technology: Windows (WebDAV, shortcut handling, fonts, BITS, PowerShell/WMI) and iOS [S3][S4][S6][S7].

gaps: The name Daffodil Gust and its Microsoft mapping to the UAE/Stealth Falcon could not be confirmed in search; the earlier source was removed.
Could not open primary documents (Citizen Lab, Check Point, Kaspersky Securelist, ESET, DOJ, Microsoft): web fetch failed on all hosts; details rest on search-result summaries of them.
Whether Microsoft's Daffodil Gust cluster fully equals vendor clusters Stealth Falcon/FruityArmor/Project Raven is unverified.
No indicators of compromise, ATT&CK mapping or infrastructure details collected.
Activity between 2019 and 2025 and any post-2021 changes to operations after DOJ action are not covered.
Exact publication dates of the 2025 secondary coverage and the Check Point original were not verified; March 2025 start date is from secondary reporting.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: operating environment includes Windows endpoints in Middle East government/defense and diplomatic networks [S6][S7]. Step 3-4 MLCOA: spear-phish with shortcut/.url files abusing WebDAV and delivering a custom implant, favoring espionage over disruption [S6]. MDCOA: further zero-day use against patched-late defense networks [S3][S6]. Candidate indicators: outbound WebDAV to unfamiliar hosts from user shortcut execution, anomalous BITS jobs [S6][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track Microsoft Patch Tuesday zero-day advisories and CVE-2025-33053 patch status (patched 2025-06-10) [S6]. Authorities: coordinate any hunt or response under existing DCO authorities; attribution remains vendor-level only [S2]. Mission assurance: prioritize patching and restrict WebDAV/shortcut execution on mission systems [S6]. Coordination: share indicators via normal vendor and partner channels.
